lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: There is no summary or target-role signal.
items.because: A recruiter may see 'Diesel Mechanic' first and assume you are pursuing marine maintenance rather than product or operations.

items.says: The experience order is incorrect.
items.because: The 2024 product internship appears after a 2025-present role and a 2018–2023 role.

items.says: The Harbor Payments section contains duplication.
items.because: Several bullets describe the same checkout/onboarding work and make the internship look padded.

items.says: A few claims need correction or clarification.
items.because: The food-app growth percentage is mathematically inconsistent, and some product metrics lack enough context to establish what you personally did.

items.says: Replace the placeholder-style website/profile URL with the actual destination if this is not already a real public profile.
items.because: Placeholder-looking contact information reduces credibility.

items.says: Consider labeling the link clearly if it is a LinkedIn profile rather than a personal website.
items.because: A recruiter should know what they will find when clicking.

items.says: Consider adding your current city and state.
items.because: Employers often screen for location, relocation, or work authorization logistics.

items.says: Add work authorization only if it is relevant to the roles or employers you are targeting.
items.because: It can remove an early screening question, but it should not be added if it is unnecessary or creates clutter.

items.says: Consider indicating completion status accurately if the degree is now completed.
items.because: Make sure the reader can immediately tell whether it is completed, in progress, or recently completed.

items.says: Add a concentration, relevant coursework, leadership role, or major academic distinction only if it directly supports product, analytics, strategy, or operations work.
items.because: A bare MBA line establishes the credential but does not help distinguish you from other MBA candidates.

items.says: Add honors, academic distinction, or relevant quantitative coursework only if genuinely strong.
items.because: Economics supports your analytical positioning, but it is not currently a differentiator by itself.

items.says: Clarify the scale, responsibility, and outcome if possible.
items.because: The metric is useful, but the current bullet does not distinguish your personal contribution from team output.

items.says: Clarify the scale, responsibility, and outcome if possible.
items.because: The metric is useful, but the current bullet does not distinguish your personal contribution from team output.

items.says: Either strengthen this bullet with measurable scope or reduce its prominence.
items.because: The maintenance activity is not especially relevant to product roles, and 'logged service records' is a low-impact task as written.

items.says: Add the scale and decision impact.
items.because: The bullet currently describes a recurring responsibility rather than an achievement.

items.says: Clarify the baseline or business consequence if available.
items.because: This is one of the best bullets in the resume because it combines a measurable outcome, process redesign, frontline collaboration, training and implementation, and a defined operating scale.

items.says: Clarify your role in designing or implementing the consensus forecast and identify the business decision affected by the improved forecast.
items.because: The main missing element is how the improvement changed inventory, capacity, purchasing, service levels, or planning decisions.

items.says: Separate or clarify the different types of work involved and clarify whether the 1,800 hours saved was measured annually and how it was calculated.
items.because: The bullet currently contains so many responsibilities that the central achievement can get lost.

items.says: Clarify what you personally owned: research, requirements, design, experiment, implementation, or launch.
items.because: The phrase 'redesigned' does not establish your level of ownership.

items.says: Clarify the experiment’s duration, success criteria, and whether the result was statistically reliable or sustained after launch.
items.because: The reader needs enough context to distinguish a robust product experiment from a temporary or noisy result.

items.says: Clarify the decision process and outcome, and why this version of Reach was appropriate.
items.because: Merely using the RICE framework is not a result.

items.says: Clarify the final decision and business outcome.
items.because: As written, it contains many activities but does not clearly show what changed because of them.

items.says: Remove or consolidate with the conversion bullet.
items.because: It repeats the result from the second bullet.

items.says: Specify your role in the presentation and whether the funding decision was directly attributable to the analysis.
items.because: It is distinct from the product discovery bullets and gives the internship an executive-facing outcome.

items.says: Clarify whether the app was built and launched by you or a team, your role in product decisions, and how the nine-tonne figure was measured.
items.because: The reader needs to understand the product’s maturity and your personal ownership.

items.says: The increase from 400 to 1,150 weekly active users is not a 150% increase.
items.because: It is a 187.5% increase relative to 400.

items.says: Separate the user research insight from the product change if necessary so the causal connection is credible.
items.because: The phrase 'chosen after 60 user interviews' may overstate causality unless the interviews clearly identified reminders as the intervention.

items.says: Describe this carefully as a 20-percentage-point increase or otherwise distinguish percentage points from relative percent growth.
items.because: Going from 75% to 95% is a 20-point increase but a 26.7% relative increase.

items.says: Clarify what analysis produced the savings estimate and what portion of the recommendation you led.
items.because: The main question is whether this was a validated savings estimate or a theoretical opportunity.

items.says: Add a measurable outcome if available, such as reduced intake time, fewer missing fields, lower abandonment, or staff hours saved.
items.because: 'Adopted' is positive but vague.

items.says: Keep only if it adds a distinct executive-communication signal; if space is limited, combine its value conceptually with the first bullet rather than repeating the pilot approval.
items.because: It overlaps with the first bullet’s statement that the client funded a pilot.

items.says: Ensure every listed skill is supported by experience or project evidence.
items.because: Skills that appear only in the skills section are less persuasive than skills demonstrated through outcomes.

items.says: Add evidence for requirements writing elsewhere only if you actually performed this work.
items.because: Requirements writing is currently not clearly demonstrated in the bullets.

items.says: Keep Jira, Amplitude, and Excel only if you can explain your level of proficiency and actual use.
items.because: Recruiters typically care more about what you accomplished with a tool than the tool name alone.

items.says: Add evidence of product analytics or funnel analysis for Amplitude, and backlog, sprint, or delivery work for Jira if you want them to carry weight.
items.because: Amplitude should connect to funnel, retention, cohort, or experiment analysis if you want it to be a meaningful signal.
